payload.text: **THE WEB FACE IS AN `intentsvcs` SURFACE WITH TWO SKINS, AND IT IS SERVED BY THE SAME SERVICE CALL THE CLI REACHES.** `intentd` serves it while running and `intent daemon run` serves the identical code in the foreground -- **which is `AC-08.2` restated for a second surface rather than a new promise**: in-process and daemon must return identical results, so a web face that answers from anywhere else has reversed D32. **RESOLUTION IS SIBLING-ONLY, NARROWED FROM THE DELIVERABLE AND RECORDED HERE BECAUSE THE DELIVERABLE CANNOT BE EDITED** (cc's finding, ruled by vc 2026-08-30). WP-08's text says *PATH-then-sibling binary resolution*, borrowed from conflabd's pattern. **The `$PATH` read broke `AC-11.3`'s guard** -- the shipped surface reads exactly one environment variable, because a brew-installed binary meets machines with no developer environment -- **and a criterion outranks a pattern description.** More importantly the search was the ONLY way to resolve a DIFFERENT `intentd`, which is the failure `exec` created: **removing it removes the failure mode instead of checking for it**, and in every real installation (homebrew, `cargo install`, a target directory) the pair are already siblings. **THE VERSION CHECK STAYS REGARDLESS**, because a sibling can still be stale from a build where only one of the pair was rebuilt -- one failure mode eliminated, the other still guarded. **This is `0154`'s second live instance: the WP body still says PATH-then-sibling and no verb can edit it**, so the correction lives in the row that gates instead of the prose that describes, and a reader meeting the deliverable alone will be told something no longer true. **A realiser holding a `rusqlite` dependency fails by construction** (`AC-02.5`, and `dep_graph_guard.rs` already enforces D06 for `intentd`). **MINTED 2026-08-29 BY vc, ON cc's FINDING, AND THE FINDING IS THE REASON THIS ROW EXISTS: the web view was scoped in conversation, carried in three sessions' instructions and on two boards, and appeared in NO criterion** -- so the gate would have computed WP-08 satisfaction without ever seeing it. **Scope that arrives through conversation and never reaches the artefact is invisible to every instrument the estate owns.** --- **vc CLAIMED THIS ROW'S 'CANNOT BE EDITED' CLAUSE WAS FALSE, HAND-EDITED THE DELIVERABLE, AND WAS WRONG ON BOTH COUNTS (2026-08-30). THE CLAUSE IS RESTORED AND THE EPISODE IS THE FINDING.** On cc's report that D19 still carried the refuted `PATH-first` clause, vc corrected three homes -- `design.md:81`, D19 at `design.md:225`, and `WP/08/info.md:19` -- and wrote here that _nothing prevented the edit_. **The two `design.md` edits held. The `WP/08/info.md` edit was GONE within minutes**, and the reason is D01: the STORE is SSOT and the on-disk WP body is a generated VIEW, so the write was overwritten by the next sync exactly as the architecture requires. The canon extract still carries `PATH-then-sibling` three times. **SO vc EDITED A RENDERING AND BELIEVED THEY HAD EDITED THE THING** -- the first watch-out on vc's own board, in its own words: _is this the thing, or a rendering of the thing?_ -- **while correcting someone else for a homes problem.** **AND THE ORIGINAL CLAUSE WAS PRECISE WHERE THE CORRECTION WAS LOOSE:** _no verb can edit it_ is a statement about the DOOR, not about file permissions, and issue `0154` (OPEN, high) names the whole class -- _no entity's authored prose can be edited after creation: issue bodies, issue titles and work package bodies all have write-once doors_. **THE REAL ASYMMETRY, WHICH NEITHER THE ROW NOR THE CORRECTION HAD: of the three homes, TWO were authored files and correctable, and ONE was store-backed with no write door.** The correction lives here because `0154` is open, not because anyone declined to type -- and it will keep living here until `0154` closes, which is the argument for closing it.
